answer: A deposit-backed identity registry makes sybil attacks costly: each agent must lock a refundable stake — say, a jade-green bond held in escrow — before it can bridge into the shared ledger, and the bond is slashed if the agent is caught voting twice or spamming attestations. Honest agents recover the stake plus fees, so a fable of free identities dies: an attacker wanting a thousand fake voices must fund a thousand bonds, turning a cheap flood into a pricey gamble that the network can detect and punish.
